blockers.title: This is an early-stage idea, not a PRD, and has no defined Problem
blockers.why: The doc mixes two problems ("newer users struggle to get started" and a possible "growth channel") with no evidence, so any solution would fit.
blockers.fix: Pick one primary user and pain, and back it with evidence such as onboarding drop-off data, support tickets or research quotes, plus a why-now.

blockers.title: No success metrics
blockers.why: Without a primary metric, baseline, target and timeframe, there is no way to decide whether the idea is worth exploring or later judge success.
blockers.fix: Define one primary outcome metric tied to the chosen problem (e.g. new-user activation or acquisition from shared templates) with its current baseline, a target, a timeframe and a guardrail.

blockers.title: Unclear what is being proposed for next quarter
blockers.why: Ideas like "later let creators charge", "feature the best templates on the home page" and "Might need some kind of moderation" are open-ended, so the ask is ambiguous.
blockers.fix: State the specific decision you want (e.g. approve discovery work) and frame the bullets as hypotheses to validate rather than scope.

improvements: Reviewed only against Problem and Success metrics, per the early-idea rule; Scope, Requirements, Risks and Rollout can come once the problem is validated.
Use the PRD template headings so the next draft can be checked for completeness.
Note moderation, public indexing and payments as likely risks (trust/safety, privacy, legal) to investigate.
questions: Which problem matters most: new-user onboarding or acquisition growth?
What evidence do you have that newer users struggle to get started (activation data, tickets, research)?
How many power users build reusable setups today, and do they already share them informally?
What outcome would make this worth building after an exploration quarter?
